tool.name: Antismash
tool.description: allows the genome-wide identification, annotation and analysis of secondary metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters
tool.command:
export PYTHONWARNINGS="ignore::FutureWarning" &&
#set $htmloutputfolder = $html.files_path #if str($infile.ext) == 'genbank': #set $file_extension = 'gb' #else #set $file_extension = $infile.ext #end if
ln -s '$infile' input_tempfile.$file_extension && #if $genefinding_gff3 ln -s '$genefinding_gff3' annotation.gff3 && #end if
#if $sideload.file #if str($sideload.format) == 'harmonize': python '$__tool_directory__/harmonize2antismash.py' '$sideload.file' sideload.json && #else ln -s '$sideload.file' sideload.json && #end if #end if
## create html folder mkdir -p '$htmloutputfolder' &&
antismash --cpus "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --databases '${databases}' --taxon '${cond_taxon.taxon}' #if $genefinding_gff3 --genefinding-gff3 annotation.gff3 #end if --genefinding-tool $cond_taxon.genefinding_tool
${cb_general} ${cb_subclusters} ${cb_knownclusters} ${smcog_trees} --tta-threshold ${tta_threshold} ${asf}
${clusterhmmer} ${fullhmmer} #if $cond_taxon.taxon == 'bacteria': $cond_taxon.tigrfam #end if
${cc_mibig} ${rre} ## always write to a local log file, it is only copied to the Galaxy ## output when the log output was selected (otherwise Galaxy would pass ## a placeholder path to --logfile) --logfile antismash.log
## Advanced options --minlength $advanced_options.minlength --hmmdetection-strictness $advanced_options.hmmdetection_strictness --cb-nclusters $advanced_options.cb_nclusters --cb-min-homology-scale $advanced_options.cb_min_homology_scale --rre-cutoff $advanced_options.rre_cutoff --rre-minlength $advanced_options.rre_minlength
#if str($advanced_options.hmmdetection_limit_to_rule_names): --hmmdetection-limit-to-rule-names '${advanced_options.hmmdetection_limit_to_rule_names}' #end if
#if $sideload.file --sideload 'sideload.json' #end if
input_tempfile.$file_extension &&
#if 'log' in $outputs: mv antismash.log '${log}' && #end if
## move the html report to the html output and all its assets into the ## html output directory, then move the data files into the results ## directory where the genbank, embl, archive and genecluster_tabular ## collections discover them. The globs may not match anything, hence the ## "|| true" guards. mv input_tempfile/index.html '${html}' && mv input_tempfile/* '${htmloutputfolder}' && mkdir -p results && ( mv '${htmloutputfolder}'/*.gbk results/ || true ) && ( mv '${htmloutputfolder}'/*.txt results/ || true ) && ( mv '${htmloutputfolder}'/*.zip results/ || true )

param.label: Sequence file in GenBank,EMBL or FASTA format
antiSMASH database

param.label: GFF3 file
param.help: Specify GFF3 file to extract features from

param.label: Taxonomic classification of input sequence
param.help: Source of DNA

param.label: Annotate with TIGRFam
param.help: Annotate clusters using TIGRFam profiles. TIGRFAMs is a collection of manually curated protein families focusing primarily on prokaryotic sequences

param.label: Full genome PFAM anotation
param.help: Each gene product encoded in the detected BGCs is analyzed against the PFAM database. Hits are annotated in the final Genbank/EMBL files. Also, selecting this option normally increases the runtime

param.label: PFAM anotation for only clusters
param.help: Run a cluster-limited HMMer analysis

param.label: Run active site finder analysis
param.help: Active sites of several highly conserved biosynthetic enzymes are detected and variations of the active sites are reported

param.label: Comparison against MIBiG database
param.help: Run a comparison against the MIBiG database

param.label: BLAST identified clusters against antiSMASH-predicted clusters
param.help: Compare identified clusters against a database of antiSMASH-predicted clusters.

param.label: KnowCluster BLAST analysis
param.help: Compare identified clusters against known gene clusters from the MIBiG database. MIBiG is a hand curated data collection of biosynthetic gene clusters, which have been experimentally characterized

param.label: Subcluster BLAST analysis
param.help: The identified clusters are searched against a database containing operons involved in the biosynthesis of common secondary metabolite building blocks (e.g. the biosynthesis of non-proteinogenic amino acids)

param.label: Run Pfam to Gene Ontology mapping module
RREFinder precision mode
param.help: Run RREFinder precision mode on all RiPP gene clusters. Many ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptide classes (RiPPs) are reliant on a domain called the RiPP recognition element (RRE). The RRE binds specifically to a precursor peptide and directs the posttranslational modification enzymes to their substrates

param.label: Analysis of secondary metabolism gene families (smCOGs)
param.help: It attempts to allocate each gene in the detected gene clusters to a secondary metabolism-specific gene family using profile hidden Markov models specific for the conserved sequence region characteristic of this family.

param.label: Lowest GC content to annotate TTA codons at
param.help: High-GC containing bacterial sequences contain the rare Leu-codon TTA as a mean for post-transcriptional regulation. Default: 0.65

param.label: Min length
param.help: Only process sequences larger than this value. Default: 1000

param.label: HMM detection strictness
param.help: Defines which level of strictness to use for HMM-based cluster detection. Default: relaxed

param.label: Limit detection to rule names
param.help: Comma-separated list of rule names to limit HMM detection to (e.g. T1PKS,terpene). Leave empty to use all rules.

param.label: Number of clusters from ClusterBlast to display
param.help: Default: 10

param.label: ClusterBlast minimum scaling factor
param.help: A minimum scaling factor for the query BGC in ClusterBlast results. Default: 0

param.label: RRE cutoff
param.help: Bitscore cutoff for RRE pHMM detection. Default: 25.0

param.label: RRE minlength
param.help: Minimum amino acid length of RRE domains. Default: 50

tool.help:
**antiSMASH** allows the rapid genome-wide identification, annotation and analysis of secondary metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters (BGCs) in bacterial and fungal genomes. It integrates and cross-links with a large number of *in silico* secondary metabolite analysis tools.
-----
# Requirements
antiSMASH needs a set of reference databases (PFAM, TIGRFam, ClusterBlast, MIBiG, RESFAM, MITE, ...) which are **not** shipped with the software package. An administrator must therefore run the **antiSMASH databases** data manager (`data_manager_antismash_database`) once; the installations it creates are offered in the *antiSMASH database* drop-down of this tool.
-----
# Input
The ideal input for antiSMASH is an annotated nucleotide file in GenBank or EMBL format.
Alternatively you can provide a FASTA file containing a single sequence - antiSMASH will generate a preliminary annotation with Prodigal and use that for the rest of the analysis. Gene annotations can also be supplied in GFF3 format.
-----
# Output
The result is an interactive HTML report with SVG graphics; the different parts of the analysis are displayed in separate panels for every gene cluster. In addition, GenBank, EMBL, gene-cluster summary and complete-result-archive outputs can be selected.
-----
# Sideloading
The *Sideloading* section allows external datasets to be added to the antiSMASH report, see the [antiSMASH sideloading documentation](https://docs.antismash.secondarymetabolites.org/sideloading/). hAMRonize summary JSON files are converted automatically to the antiSMASH format.
